newsitem.title: USA: Job growth slowed in for NYC in second half-report.
newsitem.headline: Job growth slowed in for NYC in second half-report.

text.p: New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall on Wednesday said that job growth in New York City slowed in the second half of 1996 and warned that this means welfare recipients will have a harder time finding jobs.

"Despite record profits in the volatile Wall Street sector and growth in New York City income levels, unemployment remains high. This grim job picture means that, very soon, as former welfare recipients move into the workforce, many more people will be looking for jobs than there are opportunities," the fiscal monitor said in prepared remarks.
Stiff new federal rules that became law in August impose workfare requirements for people who collect welfare.
The private sector created about 1,600 new jobs per month in the second half of 1996, down from the average monthly gain of 4,600 seen earlier in the year, McCall said.
